name: Gold
description: Gold is a ancient monetary reserve asset, supreme safe-haven vehicle, and timeless inflation hedge trusted for millennia.
supplyChain: Mined globally with main outputs from China, Russia, Australia, and Canada, then refined into high-purity bullion.
industrialUses: Primarily jewelry, aerospace electronics, dentistry, and semiconductor connectivity components due to excellent conductivity.
inflationImpact: Acts as the ultimate purchasing power protector, historically rising during high inflation or fiat currency debasement.
geopoliticalImpact: Central banks aggressively hoard gold reserves to hedge sovereign risks, rising sharply in times of international tension.
historicalImportance: The anchor of the classic Gold Standard and Bretton Woods systems, defining global money supplies until 1971.

name: Silver
description: Silver is a highly versatile dual-aspect commodity, acting both as an industrial superpower and precious monetary metal.
supplyChain: Extracted majorly as a byproduct of lead, zinc, copper, and gold mining, primarily in Mexico, Peru, and China.
industrialUses: Crucial for photovoltaic solar cells, electrical contacts, high-conductivity solders, and advanced medical equipment.
inflationImpact: Tends to outperform gold during hyper-inflationary peaks due to lower nominal price and rapid industrial demands.
geopoliticalImpact: Highly sensitive to green transition policies and global industrial development initiatives.
historicalImportance: Used extensively as historical coinage (the Pieces of Eight, silver standards) in ancient trade routes and early empires.

name: Crude Oil
description: Crude Oil is the lifeblood of global transportation, petrochemicals, and modern industrial civilizations.
supplyChain: Extracted from deep underground reservoirs, transported via pipelines and supertankers, and refined into gasoline, diesel, and plastics.
industrialUses: Combustion fuel, heavy lubricating oils, asphalt, and the universal raw base for synthetic plastics and fertilizers.
inflationImpact: Directly drives the Consumer Price Index (CPI) since transport costs cascade into every retail product price.
geopoliticalImpact: Underpins OPEC+ quotas, petrodollar recycling systems, and Middle Eastern geopolitical balances.
historicalImportance: Sparks global energy resource conflicts; the 1970s Oil Shocks transformed the Federal Reserve's monetary strategy.

name: Copper
description: Copper, nicknamed 'Doctor Copper' for its ability to gauge global macroeconomic health, is the premier infrastructure conductor.
supplyChain: Predominantly mined in Chile, Peru, and China, requiring massive energy-intensive smelting and electrolytic refining.
industrialUses: High-voltage transmission grids, residential electrical wiring, electric vehicle motors, generators, and plumbing.
inflationImpact: Reflects broad demand-pull inflation, showing immediate price surges ahead of overall manufacturing cost increases.
geopoliticalImpact: Highly vulnerable to Latin American labor strikes, Chilean mining royalties, and Chinese factory demand.
historicalImportance: The foundational element of the Bronze Age, enabling early metallic tooling and currency systems.

name: Aluminum
description: Aluminum is a lightweight, high-strength industrial metal critical for modern aviation, logistics, and structures.
supplyChain: Refined from mined Bauxite ore using the energy-heavy Hall-Héroult smelting process, concentrated near cheap electricity.
industrialUses: Aero-fuselages, vehicle engine blocks, carbonated beverage cans, power cable cores, and high-performance building frames.
inflationImpact: Acts as a pass-through for global electricity pricing due to the extreme energy required for smelting.
geopoliticalImpact: Susceptible to tariff barriers, carbon tax adjustments, and Siberian energy export constraints.
historicalImportance: Once more precious than silver, it became an industrial powerhouse in the 20th century, enabling aviation.

name: Wheat
description: Wheat is a primary agricultural staple food source, feeding over one-third of the global human population.
supplyChain: Grown in expansive temperate grain belts across North America, Russia, Ukraine, and the European Union, then milled into flour.
industrialUses: Bread, flour, livestock feeds, industrial starch bases, and biofuel ethanol production.
inflationImpact: Drives food-inflation indices directly, causing immediate cost-of-living distress when supply shrinks.
geopoliticalImpact: Black Sea blockades or export bans quickly trigger global humanitarian and political friction.
historicalImportance: The rise of agricultural empires (Rome, Egypt) was fundamentally built on securing wheat supply lines.

name: Coffee
description: Coffee is one of the world's most traded tropical agricultural commodities, driving global beverage consumption.
supplyChain: Cultivated by smallholders and expansive plantations in the equatorial 'Bean Belt' (Brazil, Vietnam, Colombia), then dry processed and exported.
industrialUses: Caffeine extraction, food flavorings, cosmetics, and universal consumer beverage packs.
inflationImpact: A discretionary bellwether, tracking retail consumer health and leisure spending patterns.
geopoliticalImpact: Friction between fair-trade cooperatives, national labor rights, and international agribusiness cartels.
historicalImportance: Spurred the European Enlightenment via London Coffee Houses, acting as centers of early financial exchanges.

name: Natural Gas
description: Natural Gas is a highly combustible hydrocarbon gas, serving as a primary thermal utility and chemical feedstock.
supplyChain: Extracted from gas-bearing shale formations, liquefied at cryogenic temperatures (LNG), and shipped across specialized ocean tankers.
industrialUses: Industrial power generation, municipal home heating systems, and the raw chemical feed for nitrogen fertilizers.
inflationImpact: Directly influences winter electricity bills and national agricultural planting costs via fertilizer prices.
geopoliticalImpact: Central to European pipeline dependencies and American LNG export geopolitical power play.
historicalImportance: Evolved from a wasted oil-refinery byproduct of early drilling into a cleaner transitional fuel of the 21st century.

name: Uranium
description: Uranium is an ultra-dense energy mineral, powering global nuclear fission reactors and zero-emission carbon-free base grids.
supplyChain: Mined heavily in Kazakhstan, Canada, and Australia, requiring specialized isotopic enrichment centrifuges.
industrialUses: Fission fuel rods in commercial nuclear power plants, medical radioisotopes, and military propulsion engines.
inflationImpact: Provides extremely stable, long-term power pricing, decoupling baseload grids from short-term fossil fuel spikes.
geopoliticalImpact: Highly guarded by nuclear non-proliferation treaties, strategic stockpiles, and East-West geopolitical alliances.
historicalImportance: The catalyst of the Atomic Age, forever changing global safety alliances, defense doctrines, and power generation.

name: Lithium
description: Lithium, the lightest metal, is the fundamental charge-carrier driving the modern global electrochemical energy transition.
supplyChain: Extracted either from high-altitude salt flats brine in South America (the Lithium Triangle) or hard-rock spodumene ore in Australia.
industrialUses: High-density Lithium-ion phone batteries, stationary energy storage grids, and electric vehicle battery packs.
inflationImpact: Directly dictates the price feasibility of electric vehicles and consumer electronic rollouts.
geopoliticalImpact: Intense global race to capture chemical refining factories, dominated heavily by China.
historicalImportance: Previously a minor industrial chemical, it became a strategic commodity of high national security importance overnight.
